subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Cupping: How Roasters Evaluate Quality
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Cupping: How Roasters Evaluate Quality.

hook.text: Cupping is the industry standard method for evaluating coffee quality. Professionals slurp loudly—it's part of the technique.

buildup.text: Coarsely ground coffee is steeped in hot water for 4 minutes. The floating crust is broken, releasing aromatic signals.

discovery.text: Tasters rate fragrance, aroma, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body, balance, sweetness, and uniformity on a 100-point scale.

twist.text: Certified Q-graders must pass 22 tests including blind tasting and flavor ID, recalibrating every 3 years.

climax.text: Cupping is both quality control and a roaster's feedback loop. Every batch is cupped before it's approved for sale.

punchline.text: Slurp, score, adjust, repeat. Cupping is where art meets accountability.

quiz.question: How often must certified Q-graders recalibrate?
